v.rationale:
I ran `php artisan test` for each: all three suites pass (impl-1: 17 tests, impl-2: 15, impl-3: 14).

The three implementations share almost the same core:
- the same FormRequest (present|nullable|string|max:30)
- the same thin controller using `update($request->validated())`
- the same JsonResource
- the same migration and the same `#[Fillable]` change

My probe tests covered:
- whitespace-only input (trimmed, then stored as null)
- an integer value (422)
- 31 multibyte characters (422)
- trimming
- PATCH with a real token
- PUT (405)
- a guest request without JSON headers

All three behave the same on every probe except the last one. There, impl-1 and impl-2 return 500 (Route [login] not defined) and only impl-3 returns 401, because it configured `redirectGuestsTo` and has a test for it. That real robustness difference puts impl-3 first.

impl-1 vs impl-2 is close. impl-1 adds a real personal-access-token test and a multibyte boundary test, and it unwraps the resource to match the spec literally. Its validation assertions are looser, though, and it has some copy-paste tests. impl-2 makes better use of datasets and asserts the actual error messages, but its mass-assignment email check is weak and it adds no coverage beyond the others. I ranked impl-1 above impl-2 for its broader, more meaningful coverage.

I deleted the probe test file from every implementation after running it.
